preston_removal_map — DRIVE polish op

• Data kinds: matrix × scalar × scalar × scalar → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.preston_removal_map(path, force, radius: 'float', k_p: 'float', shape=(128, 128), res: 'float' = 0.0001, kind: 'str' = 'flat', speed=None, times=None, spin: 'float' = 0.0, estar=None, step=None, method: 'str' = 'direct') -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import polish; polish.preston_removal_map(path, force, radius: 'float', k_p: 'float', shape=(128, 128), res: 'float' = 0.0001, kind: 'str' = 'flat', speed=None, times=None, spin: 'float' = 0.0, estar=None, step=None, method: 'str' = 'direct') -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("preston_removal_map"))

Usage

Removal-depth map [m] (shape shape, pixel res) obtained by integrating the Preston equation dh/dt = k_p p |v_rel| from the trajectory and the pressing force.

path (N, 2) is the xy of the tool centre (a NaN row lifts the tool), force is a scalar or per-row values (linearly interpolated within a segment), and either speed [m/s] or times [s] (per row). When the tool rotates with spin [rad/s], ω ẑ × (x − c) is added to the relative velocity. method="direct" accumulates over the window pixels per small segment (default step res/4). method="fft" is the convolution of "an image of the line density of the trajectory" with the normalised pressure window (preston_pressure_kernel) —— a second implementation usable only when there is no rotation, the force is constant and the speed is constant; it preserves the volume Σ h res² = k_p F × (length of the trajectory inside the map widened by half the window), excluding what spills outside the map. Raises ValueError: shape/number checks, neither speed nor times given, times not increasing, with fft: rotation / changing force / speed changing with time.
